title: Patient Payment Plan Payment Holidays
content:
**Terms for patients — deferring an installment of a Patient Payment Plan**

A payment holiday defers one installment of a Patient Payment Plan to the end of the plan only when it is requested no later than the tier's holiday notice period, in calendar days, before that installment's due date, and at most the tier's yearly allowance of payment holidays in any rolling 12 months. Days are counted backward as calendar days from the due date, the due date itself being day zero.

The rolling 12 months are the 12 calendar months ending on the date the holiday is handled; the payment holidays counted are the installments of that plan deferred as payment holidays whose due dates fall within that period.

## Questions and answers

**How late may a holiday be requested?**
On a tier with a 5-day notice period, a request for an installment due 2026-06-15 is in time on 2026-06-10 (day 5 counted backward) or earlier. A request on 2026-06-11 (day 4) is too late, and that installment is not deferred.

**How many holidays may be taken?**
No more than the tier's yearly allowance within the rolling 12 months. On a hypothetical tier allowing 1 per rolling 12 months, a plan with one deferred installment whose due date lies within the last 12 calendar months has used its allowance.

**What happens to the deferred installment?**
It moves to the end of the plan.

**Is a holiday offered on every tier?**
A holiday is available only where the tier's yearly allowance is above zero.
